posts.name: Trinith
posts.cooked:
Vilerat:

If you make items to sell on AH deflation is EDITED**** NOT good.

That’s not necessarily true. Gold only has the value in a relative sense. If you make items to sell on the AH, you’re still getting gold relative to the value the current community places on it. So sure you’re not making as much as you did before but you’re also not needing as much as you did before, so you should be fine.

I think the only way this odd deflation would have a negative impact on you is if you…

  • Only play the game to make gold, to see the number go up. It will no go up more slowly.
  • You got caught in the transition, purchasing goods pre-deflation but are now trying to sell them post-deflation.

Personally, I’m not sure I agree with the OPs conclusion. I’m not saying their wrong but I have a different theory. We’re on the end of a banwave phase and I suspect that the bots that were banned last month have now gotten to 60 and have started producing again. I’m seeing a lot of new names on the AH for the things I typically sell, which are either that new wave of bots, or just people filling the void.

I’m kind of curious to see what will happen in another week or two when Blizzard does the next banwave. If Blizzard makes a post and all of a sudden stock on the AH plummets, causing prices to rise, then my theory is potentially correct. However, if nothing changes, then I’m certainly wrong

posts.name: Trinith
posts.cooked:
Vilerat:

So if you buying stuff if helps when gold is deflating and if your selling stuff it hurts when gold is deflating.

Yes, but if you’re selling stuff so you have gold to then, in turn, buy stuff and use it, then you’re kind of existing in a short economic bubble for your server. This should describe most normal players.

The only folks who would feel any real impact of this are those whose primary gameplay is the auction house and making money.

Vilerat:

if deflation went out of control on the server. nobody would put anything up on AH

Not so… because it’s all relative to the current prices. I’ll throw down some *absolutely made up * numbers here for the purposes of example.

Let’s say I’m a miner. Prior to deflation, I farm stacks of Iron Ore and sell them on the AH for 40g a stack. I then use that gold to buy Major Mana Potions at 75g a stack. Now deflation hits and the price of my Iron Ore goes down to 10g a stack. However, the price of the Major Mana Potions I buy also falls to maybe 25g a stack. While the ratio isn’t the same, the prices of both things fell relative to one another and so the stuff I’m buying is still paid for by the stuff I’m selling. It’s still worth my while to farm Iron Ore and sell it so that I can buy Major Mana Potions.

If I’m just playing the game, the value of gold only matters relative to what I want to use it for.

The only time this might crop up as an issue is with things where the prices are fixed, such as epic mount costs. That’s a flat 1000g no matter what’s happening with the economy. Currently, even with deflation as it is, it’s very easy to afford an epic mount. If prices continue to fall it could be much harder for people in the future, similar to how it was at the start of Classic in 2019.
